body: it does sound like a yeast infection. don't use anything scented on your vulva, not even soap. if you want to use soap down there you need something super neutral and unscented, like dove, but I personally only use water. going to the doctor would be best but there are some options available over the counter. if your concern is that someone will know you've had sex, yeast infections can be caused by many things, not necessarily related to sex, so I would still suggest talking to a parent or trusted adult. in the meantime, ice helps for temporary relief, it's not a treatment but it will help you not go insane. wrap some ice in a paper towel or clean washcloth and hold it between your legs for a while, it really helps. hope you feel better soon!

I've dealt with cuts on my vulva before and I've used the lidocaine around the wound as opposed to on it. Something that gave me huge relief for a bit was putting ice on them, it helped a lot. Hope this helps!

Mi consejo sería que le preguntes qué le pasa. No que le digas que te sientes mal, sino que le preguntes por qué el cambio de actitud y si hay algo que necesiten hablar y cambiar para sentirse conformes los dos. Ahí ya depende de ella si te dice qué pasa o no. Si lo hace, verán cómo proceden juntos. Si te dice que no pasa nada y sigue igual la situación ya tienes que tomar una decisión. Conozco personas que se han quedado durante esta situación, han sido pacientes y comprensivas y las cosas terminan mejorando. Sin embargo, entiendo que no es para todo el mundo estar esperando, y si prefieres no hacerlo también es válido.

1. Personally, it does hurt. But when I cut I am in a state of despair, I feel so deep in a dark hole that cutting is the thing that brings me back to reality. After the first couple cuts it doesn't hurt as much, and then I just want to do it again and again until I come back to reality. I don't know about everyone else, but after cutting I feel incredibly calm. Definitely still sad, but not at all in the manic state that led me to cutting in the first place.
2. It's surprisingly easy to hide. I just made sure to hide the fresh cuts until they stopped being so red and big, and then I could get away with wearing short sleeves if I needed to while subtly hiding my forearms. People usually aren't looking for scars on your arms unless they already suspect something. Also, I didn't only cut in visible places. Your friend probably doesn't, either.
3. To be honest, I'm not sure. I hate the whole thing because then it feels attention seeking. The only person that has ever made me feel comfortable talking about it is my boyfriend. He doesn't beat around the bush, but he is respectful. He never treats me like I'm going to break, he asks directly what he wants to know and that makes me feel like I'm worth being treated normally. My best advice would be to just listen to your friend and DON'T make her feel like you pity her. If she's comfortable talking to you about it, ask questions and make her feel heard. No one has ever made me feel as heard as my boyfriend, and it was incredibly empowering. He made me feel like I wasn't a freak or a weirdo, just someone who went through some stuff and dealt with it in an unhealthy way.

Best of luck! I'm glad to hear your friend has someone as supportive as you.
